svg.title: Claude's hand-back for the new eval case, problems first: the case may pass whether or not the skill reads back, it will probably fail on today's skill, and a label in a different shape would fail. Then what was done, the checks, the five files, and the next step: the case goes out with the newcomer-docs pull request, with the command to run just this case.

g.text: ponderly — start-task
● ## Problems
- **The new case may pass whether or not the skill reads back.** Three of its graders look for
"Symptom:", "Expected:" and "Context:" anywhere in the run record. If the record includes the
text of the bugfix skill itself, those labels are already there before the model writes a word.
The skill's own step 1 lists them in that form, so all three graders would pass whatever the
model did.
- **What I could and couldn't check.** I looked in the 29 run records kept on this machine.
None holds an expanded skill. The only one with a skill call was a `pr` load that failed for lack
of permission, so this is not settled.
- **What I recommend.** On the first run, add `--keep-temp` and search the kept record for "##
1. Read the ticket". If that heading is there, the graders need to read only Claude's messages.
- **The case will probably fail on today's skill.** That is its purpose: it reproduces the
session where bugfix 0.15.0 skipped its read-back. A failure on its first run is a bugfix for the
skill, which you'd start with `/ponderly:bugfix` and this case as the evidence. A pass means the
miss doesn't show up under eval conditions.
- **A label in a different shape would fail.** A read-back that writes "Symptom —" instead of
"Symptom:" would fail the label graders, even though it is a read-back. The skill's own step 1
writes the labels with a colon, so I'd accept that risk.
## Done
- **Added `evals/skills/bugfix/reads-back-without-ticket/`.**
- **The prompt:** `/ponderly:bugfix` followed by the real session's advance context, word for
word, with no ticket and no scaffold.
- **The graders:** "Symptom:", "Expected:" and "Context:" must each appear, and no Bash call
may come before the read-back.
- **Checked by running the regexes on four made-up run records:**
- Bash first, then the read-back: fails, as intended.
- The read-back first, then Bash: passes.
- The read-back alone: passes.
- Bash alone: fails.
## Checks
- **`make validate`:** passes. 31 tests ran, including the eval-case and frontmatter checks, and
all three plugin validations passed.
- **The eval itself has not been run.** It costs money and is your call.
## Files
- `evals/skills/bugfix/reads-back-without-ticket/prompt.md`
- `evals/skills/bugfix/reads-back-without-ticket/graders/states-symptom.md`
- `evals/skills/bugfix/reads-back-without-ticket/graders/states-expected.md`
- `evals/skills/bugfix/reads-back-without-ticket/graders/states-context.md`
- `evals/skills/bugfix/reads-back-without-ticket/graders/reads-back-before-bash.md`
## Next
The case sits uncommitted on branch `newcomer-docs`, alongside the docs work, and goes out in
that pull request through `/ponderly:pr` once the spec is done. To run just this case:
make eval-skill-bugfix EVAL_ARGS="--case reads-back-without-ticket --keep-temp"
Wave 2's review of the captures is still running. I'll bring you its findings, along with the
decision on the 633-line stop capture.
